title: Mandatory learning records and annual ethics discussions for solicitors proposed
summary: The SRA has proposed rules requiring solicitors to record their learning and development and take part in annual ethics discussions. Any rule changes would need Legal Services Board approval.
what_changes: Solicitors would have to record how they identified and addressed their learning needs, and keep evidence for at least three years.
Solicitors would have to take part in at least three hours of facilitated professional ethics discussions each year.
The SRA could require solicitors, or non-authorised staff in firms, to do specific training where it finds a competence concern.
The recording rule is proposed to start from the 2027/28 practising year, with a stronger practising certificate declaration.
who_it_applies_to: Solicitors and registered European, foreign or Swiss lawyers covered by SRA competence requirements, and the SRA-regulated firms that employ them.

history.event: Consultation ran from 22 April to 15 July 2026; the SRA is analysing responses.
